newsitem.title: FRANCE: Generale des Eaux's Cegetel to give profit.
newsitem.headline: Generale des Eaux's Cegetel to give profit.

text.p: Cie Generale des Eaux chairman Jean-Marie Messier said on Wednesday that the company would post an exceptional profit due to the creation of telecommunications unit Cegetel.
Messier did not say how big the profit would be but analysts have said they expect it to be between five billion and six billion francs.

Cegetel, which Messier has said he hopes to build into France's second-largest telecommunications operator after France Telecom, will be 50 percent owned by Generale des Eaux, 25 percent by British Telecommunications PLC, 15 percent by SBC Communications Inc and 10 percent by Mannesmann AG .
Messier said Cegetel should represent 15 percent of Generale des Eaux's turnover and 25 percent of its cash flow by 2003.
Messier said he hoped Cegetel's turnover would rise to 8.6 billion francs in 1997, 12.9 billion in 1998, 25.2 billion in 2000 and 38.6 billion in 2003.
Generale des Eaux's telecommunication business has turnover of about three billion francs, Messier said.
